title: Victorian election 2026 live: voters head to the polls as Coalition seeks to topple Labor – latest news
summary: Follow live updates today and results tonight as Labor’s Ben Carroll and Liberal leader Jess Wilson seek victory in Victoria’s state election

blocks.text: Key events
Jess Wilson and Ben Carroll ‘confident’ as they cast votes

My colleague Benita Kolovos has informed me that the premier, Ben Carroll, voted at his old primary school St Christophers in Airport West, while the Liberal leader, Jess Wilson, voted at Our Lady of Good Counsel primary school in Deepdene.
Wilson told a reporter at the polling booth she was “confident of the victories statewide today” and downplayed what it would mean for her to become the first elected female premier in Victoria.
She said:
double quotation markIt’s not about me. If I’m given that honour, we’re absolutely ready and I’m ready. But this is about Victorians and fixing this state.
Carroll told reporters he was “fighting every day” for the state. He said:

double quotation markI am confident because I’m getting that message. I’ve got it all day yesterday. People do feel like they’ve been sold down the river by the Liberal party, after 50% of Victorians voted, to come out with a radical privatisation agenda around kinder, renewables and water. People do feel very angry about that.

blocks.caption: Ben Carroll and his wife, Fiona Rothville, and their daughter, Madeline, at St Christopher's primary school in Airport West. Photograph: Con Chronis/AAP

blocks.text: Who are the leaders?

Going into the election, the Labor government is led by the premier, Ben Carroll. Carroll, who has only led Labor since late July, became leader after a spill against Jacinta Allan. Allan herself only became leader after the resignation of Daniel Andrews, who led Labor to the “Dan-slide” of 2022.

Victorian Labor has never won an election after changing leaders and this time they have done it twice. But Carroll has made an effort to distance himself from his predecessors saying, “I will do things differently”.

blocks.caption: The Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, outside the Olivia Newton-John Cancer Research Institute in Heidleberg, in Melbourne, on Tuesday. Photograph: James Ross/AAP

blocks.text: Jess Wilson is the Liberal leader, hoping to become the next premier. She became leader after a period of instability in the Victorian Liberal party that saw three leaders since the last election.
If she wins, she will be the youngest person to lead Victoria and the first woman to be elected premier. (Both Joan Kirner and Jacinta Allan became premier after their leaders resigned).

blocks.caption: Jess Wilson during a visit to an early voting centre at Heidelberg Scots Uniting Church in Melbourne on Tuesday. Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAP

blocks.text: There’s also the minor parties.
The Victorian Greens are led by Ellen Sandell. In 2014, she became the first Greens MP to be elected to Victoria’s lower house after campaigning against local toll roads.

Sandell hopes to take a page from progressive leaders around the world such as the New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani. At the News24 leaders’ debate, Sandell outperformed Ben Carroll, according to an audience poll.

blocks.caption: The Victorian Greens leader, Ellen Sandell, in Melbourne. Photograph: Con Chronis/AAP

blocks.text: Leading the insurgent One Nation is Warren Pickering. He is running in the marginal Labor seat of Pakenham in Melbourne’s outer east. The former Australian army combat engineer was also a unsuccessful One Nation Senate candidate.
At the News24 leaders’ debate, Pickering was outperformed by Sandell but audiences still preferred him over Carroll.

blocks.caption: The One Nation Victoria leader, Warren Pickering. Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAP

blocks.text: What the polls say
The Coalition is poised to win 55 of 88 lower-house seats according to a YouGov poll of more than 4300 voters, commissioned by the Herald Sun and News24 and published on election eve.
One Nation would gain 12 seats and the Greens would add five more MPs to their pack of three, according to the analysis conducted between 6 and 23 November.
A Newspoll reported by The Australian late on Thursday had the Coalition extending to a 15-point lead over Labor on a two-party preferred basis.
The Coalition’s lead of 57.5% to Labor’s 42.5% compares with the Coalition’s 55-45 lead in October before the election campaign began.
If the polls are correct the Victorian Greens will have their most successful campaign on record, gaining between 13% and 17% of primary votes.
The party leader, Ellen Sandell, received the second-highest approval rating among undecided voters during the campaign’s only four-way leaders debate on 17 November.
– Australian Associated Press
Welcome
Good morning, and welcome to the Victorian election live blog.
I’m Josh Taylor and I will be taking you through until later this afternoon.

Going into today, polls suggest the Coalition will comfortably win majority government, while Labor faces an electoral wipeout after 12 years in government, with suggestions the premier, Ben Carroll, could lose his own seat.
More than 2.2 million people had already voted as of Friday, according to the Victorian Electoral Commission, meaning nearly half of those eligible have already cast their vote.
Just as well, too, given the weather in Victoria today. Those democracy sausage sandwiches will be a little wet today with all the rain.

There is a flood warning for parts of west, central and north-east Victoria, with possible minor flooding from Saturday morning for rivers including the Yarra. Rain is likely to continue throughout the day, easing into the evening with up to 30mm of rain expected in Melbourne.
Now let’s get into it.
